subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should the repeated provider tool-schema normalization problem be fixed by refreshing and landing the tactical cache in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664, or should it wait for the broader prepared-runtime migration tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77700?
rationale: Current source supports the bug report and an open fix exists, but root policy also pushes hot paths toward prepared runtime facts rather than scattered caches, so the permanent fix shape is a maintainer product/architecture choice.

options.title: Refresh the focused cache PR
options.body: Update or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 so the bounded provider-normalization cache lands with its existing custom-hook and closure-freshness proof.

options.title: Fold into prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77700 and solve it by moving prepared tool/provider facts earlier instead of adding the tactical cache.

options.title: Defer for live Google proof
options.body: Wait for a live Google/Gemini reproduction of the anti-abuse symptom, accepting that the source-proven repeated normalization and reported OOM pressure remain unresolved for now.

recommendation.title: Refresh the focused cache PR
recommendation.body: Update or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 so the bounded provider-normalization cache lands with its existing custom-hook and closure-freshness proof.

likelyOwner.reason: mcaxtr owns the overlapping prepared-runtime tracking issue, which is the main architectural alternative to the tactical cache.
